canonical_policy.name: No CQRS/mediator/VSA by default
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not introduce CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization unless explicitly approved.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Approval covers any mediator library, not just names; package-review Accepted-name mechanics already BF0047. No new package exception interpretation inferred.

| `.claude/hooks/claude-hook.mjs` | `pre-bash` (fails closed): blocks npm/pnpm/yarn force/legacy-peer flags and `dotnet add/remove … reference` / `dotnet reference add/remove` before they run, also behind global options such as `--prefix`, `--dir`, `--cwd` · `post-bash`, after successful and failed shell calls: compares the active worktree's manifests (tracked and untracked, not ignored) with a per-worktree snapshot kept in the Git directory, validates added and changed manifests, reports removals and moves, routes dependency and project-reference changes; the first observation of a worktree validates every manifest · `post-edit`: manifest checks, dependency and reference-change routing, product-input reminder, structure check after instruction edits · `stop`: co-change reminders (seed, migrations, tests, custom settings) repeated only when the changed files or their content differ, never loops |

**Owned here:** CQRS handlers, mediator-based organization (with any mediator library), and Vertical Slice Architecture are not adopted. Introducing them requires approval.

- Frontend: do not add NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind, or additional form, component, or state-management libraries by default; use built-in Angular capabilities first and add an extra library only for a concrete need.
- Backend: mediator libraries such as MediatR or Kommand (mediator-based organization is not adopted — `1-architecture/overview.md`); another mapping framework without approval.

MediatR, CQRS handler trees, Vertical Slice Architecture, Domain Events, Specifications, SharedKernel, BuildingBlocks, EventBus, messaging, microservices, Kubernetes, cloud-specific projects, state-management frameworks, Docker, generic `Common`/`Helpers`/`Utils` directories — governed by `1-architecture/overview.md`, `code-organization.md`, and `3-project/decisions.md`.

canonical_policy.name: Controllers are thin HTTP entry points
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: ASP.NET Core Controllers are the default HTTP entry point; they bind/validate input, invoke Application services, and translate outcomes to HTTP responses.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Thin HTTP input/outcome responsibilities match; stronger explicit-request Minimal API condition already BF0022; avoid endpoint-filter validation in Controller project explicit.

context_quotes:
- HTTP entry points are thin: they bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application services, and translate Application outcomes into HTTP responses.
- Entry points must not contain business logic, access the persistence context or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.

- Api entry points are ASP.NET Core Controllers (approved in `3-project/decisions.md`). Do not create Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
- `IActionResult`, `ActionResult<T>`, `ProblemDetails`, `HttpContext`, `ClaimsPrincipal`, `IHttpContextAccessor`, and `StatusCodes` are web-framework transport types: they stay in Api and never appear in Application or Domain contracts.

|---|---|
| Backend platform | .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Controllers. Moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval. |
| Persistence | EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server (`Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer`); used only inside Infrastructure per `1-architecture/persistence-boundary.md`. |
Minimal API version groups in a Controller project; a new version for every implementation change.
Avoid inconsistent anonymous error objects and validation coupled to Minimal API endpoint filters in a Controller-based project.

canonical_policy.name: Program is composition root
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Program.cs is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Composition root plus permission to register outer implementations match. Do-not-shorten Program by arbitrary relocation and Swagger Api/composition placement already explicit.

context_quotes:
- `Program.cs` in Api is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations (default).
- Keep registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence and adapters, and Api remains the composition root (default).

|---|---|
| Domain | `backend/<Name>.Domain/` |
| Application | `backend/<Name>.Application/` |
| Infrastructure | `backend/<Name>.Infrastructure/` |
| Api | `backend/<Name>.Api/` (contains `Program.cs`) |
Use `Contracts/` only when transport-specific contracts provide a concrete boundary benefit. Do not move arbitrary code out of `Program.cs` only to make it shorter.
Keep Swagger configuration in Api/composition. Built-in `AddOpenApi()` / `MapOpenApi()` is not the template default when the requirement is Swagger UI.

context_quotes:
- The persistence framework is an Infrastructure implementation detail. Use it normally inside Infrastructure and take advantage of its capabilities, but do not leak its concepts into Application.

canonical_policy.name: Unit of Work is commit boundary
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use IUnitOfWork as the normal commit boundary for an Application use case; repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Application commit decision and repository staging match; shared scoped DbContext delegation explicit. Bulk tracked-state transaction cautions and no cross-UoW tracked-entity cache are separately registered.

context_quotes:
- `IUnitOfWork` is the normal commit boundary of an Application use case: repositories stage changes, and Application Services decide when to commit (default).
- Repositories participating in one use case must share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context. Repositories are injected explicitly into their consumers; `IUnitOfWork` must not become a repository container or service locator.

- Entity mappings live in Infrastructure as `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes, keeping persistence configuration out of Domain entities where practical (prefer).
- The Infrastructure implementation of `IUnitOfWork` delegates to the same scoped `DbContext` that the use case's repositories share.
- An Infrastructure-only `Repository<TEntity>` base class may expose protected helpers to concrete repositories; concrete repositories may use the full EF Core API internally.
Caching EF tracked entities across Unit of Work boundaries; Redis added merely because the application caches.

Also check proportionality: abstraction count justified by actual complexity, and no consequential pattern without approval. Never report a violation merely because the code differs from a pattern this architecture has not adopted (`1-architecture/overview.md`).

EF Core's `DbContext` already provides change tracking and unit-of-work behavior; `IUnitOfWork` is the Application-facing abstraction over that commit boundary.

`ExecuteUpdateAsync`/`ExecuteDeleteAsync` run directly against the database and bypass change tracking; do not mix them casually with tracked entities for the same rows, and understand their transaction implications.
